findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility when the inspector arrived. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. The inspector suggests more employees taking the CFPM class to ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Observed that the employee health reporting agreements were not signed by all employees. During the inspection all employees signed the agreement. Ensure that new employees sign the agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. During the inspection the sanitizer bucket was re-made testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizing concentrations are always testing at the correct concentration (50-200 ppm (Cl)).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the rice cooker on the counter was hot holding rice between 125-130F. The PIC stated that the rice was cooked at 12 pm. The rice was put under a time-as-control policy and any leftover rice will be discarded at 4 pm. The PIC was instructed to closely monitor the temperature of the rice cooker to ensure that it is functioning properly. The inspector will return on 12/8/2025 to check that the rice is being hot held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed the facility was using Always Save Bleach that does not have an EPA registration. The PIC was educated that bleach must have an EPA registration indicating that it is safe for food contact surfaces. During the inspection Chlorox bleach with an EPA registration was brought to the facility. Ensure that bleach for sanitizing solutions always has an EPA registration.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Observed employees had not signed the employee health reporting agreements. The PIC was reminded that all employees must read and sign the agreement. During the inspection employees signed the agreement. Ensure that all new employees sign the reporting agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the fans in the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.
